rationale: The generalized overlay slot is what @pulp/react's <View overlay> prop, and therefore every imported or materialized design's popover, claims. Deciding what a press or an Escape means for it was implemented once per platform host, and the four copies drifted in four different directions. The standalone macOS host read the process-global View::active_overlay_ shim mirror, which names the most recent claim anywhere in the process, so with two windows open a press in one dismissed the other's popover. The web/WASM host read the same mirror and carried a further reduced copy: a press inside the overlay was never routed into the overlay's own subtree, so an absolutely-positioned popover child lost the click to whatever later sibling occupied that pixel, and an overlay that opted to consume the dismissing press did not get to, so one click both closed the popover and mutated the control underneath it. Neither DAW plugin host had an Escape path at all, because both hand the keyboard back to the DAW whenever nothing in their tree holds focus, which is the ordinary state while a popover is open. This change gives the policy one implementation. core/view/src/overlay_dismissal.cpp now owns route_press_to_active_overlay (moved unchanged out of pointer_dispatch.cpp), route_context_press (moved unchanged), the new route_escape_to_active_overlay, which carries the whole Escape ordering of modal then open ComboBox dropdown then generalized slot that the standalone host previously spelled out inline, and the new non-mutating root_has_dismissible_overlay. pointer_dispatch.hpp includes the new header so every existing caller still compiles. The macOS plugin host additionally lets an embedded editor hold the DAW keyboard for exactly as long as a dismissible overlay is open, because otherwise Escape never reaches -keyDown: and the routing would be unreachable; keys the editor does not consume are still forwarded to the host, and -keyDown: re-syncs so the keyboard returns the moment the overlay closes. No pointer phase, capture, focus, wheel, scroll, or layout contract changed and no existing signature changed meaning. This is Pulp-only. The defect shape is an artifact of how Pulp owns the seam between a native host and a retained view tree: Pulp asks each platform host to synthesise input delivery itself, so a routing rule that lives only in prose is dropped by the next host that implements the phase. A Vellum-native retained UI kernel should own input delivery as one pipeline in which overlay dismissal is a property of the pipeline rather than a per-host convention, so this is not a shape Vellum should inherit. There is no named immutable Vellum framework commit being backported here, and this records no Vellum acknowledgement.
